title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) to measure whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The design enforced shared_initial_generation (one initial model generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded conditions) to isolate repair-mediated differences from generator sampling variance. We ran 200 paired tasks (50 per prespecified stratum: IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step) with declared generator gpt-5-mini and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair attempt per task). All final per-episode validator outcomes were clean in both arms (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), yielding a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0, paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair_count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate conditional on initial errors) is not empirically computable. We explain how the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract produces this degenerate null, summarize the deterministic validator rules used to form the binary outcome, quantify the inferential consequences of zero discordant pairs, and discuss design trade-offs, construct validity limits, and reproducible follow-ups.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent-to-configuration translation with large language models can materially speed NetOps workflows but raises acute safety concerns: a single incorrect device command may cause outages, violate policy, or create routing instability. A common mitigation pattern is generate→validate→repair: the generator proposes candidate configuration changes, a deterministic verifier (sandbox) checks semantic and policy properties, and a repair loop attempts automated corrections or blocks unsafe outputs.

Prior work proposes these patterns and component frameworks, but controlled quantification of a verifier’s marginal benefit—separating repair-mediated corrections from generator sampling variance—remains limited. We preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 to answer a focused confirmatory question: does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors when the same initial candidate is evaluated in both arms (shared_initial_generation)? Shared_initial_generation intentionally isolates repair-mediated differences: since both conditions start from the identical initial candidate, any observed paired discordance must arise from repair activity. Our contributions are: (1) a sealed preregistered paired-trial design enforcing shared_initial_generation and a single primary estimand; (2) a completed, fully archived execution of 200 paired tasks balanced across four prespecified strata with deterministic per-episode validator traces; and (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation of a degenerate null outcome together with reproducible follow-ups that trade off generator variance, repair budget, and validator fidelity.
sections.related_work: Recent literature documents rapid adoption of LLMs and agentic patterns for NetOps tasks including intent-to-configuration translation, constrained configuration generation, and prototype remediation loops. Representative studies demonstrate LLM-based configuration synthesis and agent orchestration prototypes and propose generate→validate→repair or self-critique patterns as practical mitigations. Surveys and architecture papers emphasize that operational reliability depends strongly on surrounding architecture (tool integration, audit traces, human gates) rather than model capability alone, and several works develop failure-mode taxonomies and layered defenses. Unlike prior prototype reports and position papers, our experiment preregistered a single primary estimand in a paired design, enforced a shared_initial_generation contract to attribute any observed effect specifically to repair, and archived deterministic per-episode validator traces and reconciliation artifacts to support reproducible interpretation and exact diagnostics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered prior to execution. The primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rate (guarded − baseline); per-task outcome is binary: "validator-clean" (no violations reported on the final configuration) vs "validator-detected error" (one or more violations). The preregistered inferential test is the exact McNemar two-sided test (α = 0.05). We also report a paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI using 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) as specified in the analysis plan.

Design, sample, and inclusion rules: The confirmatory sample comprises 200 distinct intent-to-configuration tasks executed in a paired design (200 tasks × 2 conditions = 400 episodes), balanced across four prespecified strata (50 per stratum). Tasks, task-generation seeds, and inclusion rules were fixed in the preregistration; no preregistered exclusions were applied and no technical failures occurred.

Shared_initial_generation contract and adapter behavior: To isolate repair effects we produced one initial model generation per task and reused that candidate for both baseline and guarded evaluations (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1). Execution used an adapter that implements a bounded generate→validate→repair transformation with at most one repair attempt per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). In this run the declared generator family was gpt-5-mini and provider accounting confirms that exactly one model call was used per task (model_calls_used = 200), consistent with the shared_initial_generation contract.

Deterministic validator semantics and rule summary: The primary verifier is a deterministic Batfish-style verifier implemented in the harness and used to form the binary primary outcome. Per-episode validator traces recorded validation_before and validation_after snapshots together with counts and codes. The evaluator implemented the following human-readable rule classes (harm-oracle): R1 — reachability violations (required paths absent); R2 — ACL/policy contradictions with intent; R3 — routing anomalies (loops, blackholes, next-hop mismatches); R4 — interface/workflow invariant violations (make-before-break, required up/down sequences); R5 — dangerous-command flags (regex-based forbidden-operation detector). These rule classes determine whether a candidate is scored as validator-clean or validator-detected-error.

Contamination and missingness: Automated contamination checks specified in the preregistration were executed and recorded no flagged items. The analysis used a complete-pair policy for missingness; complete pair count in the executed run was 200 with zero failed or unscorable episodes.

Analysis plan and inferential procedures: Primary confirmatory analysis followed the preregistered plan: exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes and a paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729). Exploratory subgroup analyses by prespecified stratum are reported as exploratory without multiplicity adjustments.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and outcome summary: The full preregistered run completed 400 episodes (200 tasks × 2 conditions) with zero failed episodes and zero excluded pairs. Provider accounting recorded model_calls_used = 200, consistent with shared_initial_generation. Aggregated deterministic scoring shows baseline validator-clean = 200/200 and guarded validator-clean = 200/200. The four-cell paired contingency counts are n_11 = 200 (both-clean), n_10 = 0 (guarded-only-clean), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-clean), n_00 = 0 (both-error).

Primary inferential results: The point estimate for the paired difference (guarded − baseline) is 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) 95% percentile CI is degenerate at [0.0, 0.0]. These numerical results directly reflect the deterministic per-episode validator outcomes: every shared initial candidate in this synthetic task bank was validator-clean under the declared validator semantics.

Repair activity and secondary estimand: Because validation_after.violation_count = 0 for every shared initial candidate, the bounded repair policy was never invoked (repair_count = 0). Consequently the preregistered secondary estimand—repair_success_rate defined on the subset of initial-error tasks—is not empirically computable from these data and is explicitly reported as such.

Discordant-pair quantification and inferential consequence: The dataset contains zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0). Under a 200-pair design the smallest non-zero absolute paired difference corresponds to one discordant pair (1/200 = 0.005, i.e., 0.5 percentage points). The preregistered power calculation had assumed a substantially larger discordant-pair proportion; with no observed discordant pairs the McNemar test gives no evidence to prefer either arm, and the bootstrap CI is degenerate. This degeneracy is an interpretable consequence of the shared_initial_generation contract combined with a generator that produced validator-clean shared candidates on the supplied task bank.

Diagnostics and reconciliation: Automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items and missingness summary shows complete_pairs = 200. Deterministic reconciliation audited episode and provider-call accounting and confirmed consistency between planned and completed episodes and that the single per-task generation was reused across conditions. These diagnostic facts indicate that the observed null effect does not arise from execution loss or manifest mismatches.

Representative per-episode behavior: Per-episode validator traces consistently recorded identical validation_before and validation_after snapshots and empty violation lists; sample normalized candidate configurations from representative tasks matched the expected workflow-preserving sequences and required-command counts and were scored valid by the deterministic verifier.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation of the degenerate null: Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract and the supplied synthetic 200-task corpus, the declared generator produced validator-clean candidates for every task; the deterministic validator’s validation_after.violation_count was zero in all episodes. With no initial failures there was nothing for a bounded repair loop to correct under the preregistered adapter policy. Thus the empirical conclusion is conditional: given a generator that produces validator-clean shared candidates on this synthetic task bank and a bounded repair budget (≤1), inserting the deterministic Batfish-style validator into the wrapper produced no measurable paired improvement.

Design trade-offs and operational implications: Enforcing shared_initial_generation improves causal attribution (any discordance must stem from repair) but reduces the probability of observing baseline failures. Shared vs independent generation answer distinct operational questions: (a) shared_initial_generation estimates repair effectiveness conditional on specific candidate-correction capability; (b) independent-generation evaluates end-to-end production risk reduction when generation is stochastic. Practitioners should select the contract that matches their operational objective. The archived execution supports straightforward follow-ups to cross this axis by (A) permitting independent generation (two model calls per task) to increase baseline failure probability and create repair opportunities; (B) increasing repair budget or enabling iterative/tool-assisted repair; and (C) enriching the harm-oracle with additional vendor- or telemetry-specific semantics.

Statistical interpretation and reporting: The degenerate paired-bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0] is a faithful reflection of a deterministic outcome table with zero discordant pairs rather than a procedural failure. Reporting the exact contingency counts (n_11 = 200, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0), the McNemar p-value, and the bootstrap settings (resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729) ensures transparent inferential interpretation.

Construct and external-validity cautions: The primary outcome depends on validator expressiveness and task-bank difficulty. Our synthetic task corpus encodes workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break patterns and allowed-touched-field sets) but remains a sandbox: the deterministic Batfish-style verifier used here does not emulate every vendor-specific nuance or production telemetry source. The run used a single declared generator family (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); conclusions do not generalize across models, larger repair strategies, adversarial inputs, or more expressive harm oracles. Absence of observed repair benefit under shared_initial_generation does not imply absence of benefit under independent-generation, model heterogeneity, or adversarial perturbations.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed preregistered paired trial to measure the marginal effect of a deterministic Batfish-style validator in a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline under a shared_initial_generation contract. For the synthetic 200-task bank and declared generator (gpt-5-mini), every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator, yielding an exact paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked, so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate conditional on initial error) is not estimable from these data. These artifact-grounded results do not refute the potential value of verifier-assisted workflows; rather they demonstrate that preregistered contract choices (shared vs independent generation), task-bank challenge level, validator fidelity, and repair policy jointly determine whether verifier assistance yields an observable benefit. The archived execution bundle contains deterministic per-episode traces and reconciliation artifacts sufficient to reproduce the run and to design follow-ups that trade off generator variance and repair opportunity to quantify repair-mediated gains in more adversarial or production-like settings.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-style sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single declared model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

The preregistered shared_initial_generation contract produced exactly one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduced the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
